# 24小时内获得百万曝光和数百付费客户

**发布时间：2026-01-29**

你有没有想过，一次发布能做到多大？

Rox Codes做到了24小时内数百万曝光、数百付费客户。

而他之前5年的创业，全失败了。

## 五年失败，终于等到这一天

Rox Codes为创作者建工具超过5年。

他大学学CS，然后试着做 restaurant 初创公司。

Failed。

所以他卖掉一切，搬到泰国，做了几年 digital nomad。

在那段时间，他成了全职Twitch streamer，每天live coding 8小时。

他为Twitch streamers建工具。

那也失败了。

然后他开始为YouTubers建ThumbnailTest.com。

MrBeast团队找到他，他在那里工作了一会儿，为他们建工具。

离开Beast后，他在5位数MRR时卖掉了ThumbnailTest。

那是2024年初，YouTube发布 competitor 前4个月。

Shortly after that，The Diary of a CEO的Steven Bartlett reach out 说"让我们一起建点什么"。

他们 messed around with ideas for a few months 然后想到了Flightcast——

video-first podcast hosting。

他们2025年10月正式推出。

用 flat SaaS subscription 加 small 广告 cut。

Already，revenue高于ThumbnailTest ever was。

## 简单但 awesome

Rox love 为创作者 building。

多年在这个 space，他终于能 tell when there's something missing。

有很多"创作者工具"，但很少有做不同事情的。

只是 lots of AI。

他想建感觉 simple 的生意——explicitly not 在 core 使用AI，

只是在一个或两个 feature 里。

他选择 video podcasting 因为它是个 super annoying problem——

大文件、多次上传、analytics 分散在许多平台。

它 felt like 尝试建东西的 fun space。

If he do this right，Flightcast should feel dead simple but awesome。

## 很多次迭代

它基于NextJS、Cloudflare、Go backend 做一些 media stuff，OVH server。

And they finally moved to Planetscale for the DB，thank God。

Building it took a lot of iterations。

Surprisingly awkward to mix a lot of these APIs。

And he had to redo the data architecture a bunch of times too。

Letting people do five posts at once sounds great，but man it sucks to build。

If he did it again，he'd limit v1.0 to just one awesome feature——likely analytics——

and ship that before taking on additional complexity of publishing，etc。

And even if he kept expanded feature set for v1.0，

he would finish one at a time instead of building several things at once。

Once that was done，they started bringing on beta users and building against feedback。

The rule was——they can't launch until it's good enough for The Diary of a CEO。

## 成为CEO

This time he's the CEO，which is really unusual for him。

He can't just go into code for 12 hours anymore。

It's harder to lock in when you can't just go into code for 12 hours。

And he's had to learn to feel good about his work even when it isn't as tangible or straightforward。

Then there's managing a team。

They got seed funding for the first time in his life，so they brought in a couple of people smarter than him。

He's used to working by himself。

He had no idea how to run a team or build a product from scratch with others。

And it was especially difficult because he was the one with most of the context，

but half of building is learning what works。

Honestly，if he had to start over，he probably would have delayed bringing on a team until the foundation was done。

He's so proud he gets to have this moment in his journey at all，but damn it's tough。

## 预填充分销

After fighting distribution for a long time，he came to understand the creator world，

and he realized that he needed a partner with the right audience and mindset。

With this business，partnering with Steve essentially prefilled the distribution。

So here's some advice：Partner with a creator。

If you find the right one，it'll be the best decision you ever make。

They had probably the largest launch of his entire life on LinkedIn + PR in podcast news outlets。

The entire expanded Flight team posted on LinkedIn on the same day——

their entire network is podcast people。

They had millions of impressions and hundreds of paying customers by the end of it。

It was a multi-year "overnight success" kind of day。

Since then，growth has been pretty straightforward。

Lots of podcasts recommending Flightcast to friends。

And agencies adding more and more shows。

But they have some upcoming big marketing strategies。

He'll be on podcasts，they're launching an affiliate program，

and they'll be giving podcasters discounts for putting Flightcast ads into their shows。

## 和比你成功的人交谈

What helped him most was talking to people who are a good bit more successful than him about very specific problems：

people problems，hiring problems，mindset problems，running a tech team，etc。

There's a lot written about everything to do with indie hacking，

but less so when things get bigger。

Or at least——the writing about it is more generic。

It's harder to learn from。

Getting coffee with a friend who runs a company 1-2 stages beyond his has been a blessing again and again。

## 比任何人都更在乎

Here's where to start：

Find a bunch of people who make decent money，but not enough people pay attention to。

Find what they're using right now。

Replace one thing——make your entire first build just one amazing feature。

He took ThumbnailTest straight out of TubeBuddy，

and over many months made his A/B tester 5x better。

He made it an easy，obvious choice for anyone using TubeBuddy to switch to ThumbnailTest。

You can do the same。

Just care way more about one small problem than anyone else has。

## 未来的目标

He wants Flightcast to be his magnum opus。

He wants to build something so good it redefines the expectations people have for what a tool like this can do。
